branch: maptiles-native - NOT wired into the Next.js app
deterministic: no clock and no network: this file is a pure function of the inputs digested below, plus the z6 tiles on disk - which of them exist (which tie-breaks boss layer routing) and how much art each one carries (which is the whole of "sheets"). Two rebuilds are byte-identical on any day, so a diff between two outputs always means an input changed. This replaces the wall-clock "generated" date, which made that guarantee expire at midnight and answered a question nobody asks.

frame.world: worldX = px + 7040 ; worldZ = 16512 - py ; 1 master px = 1 world unit
frame.levelPx: at zoom z, screen-space position is px / 2^(6-z)
frame.tileInk: sheets[].ink is a base64 BYTE table over the sheet's OWN tx/ty bounding box at z6, row-major: byte i is tile (tx[0] + i % w, ty[0] + floor(i / w)) with w = tx[1] - tx[0] + 1. Its value is round(255 * the fraction of that tile a user can tell apart from the page behind it) - 0 both where no .webp exists and where one exists but carries no visible art, which are the same thing to anyone looking at the screen. sheets[].inked counts the non-zero bytes and is the check a reader makes on the table, as popcount === tiles was on the bitset this replaced; sheets[].tiles and .density still count FILES, because the 404 story is about requests, not art.

sources.bonfire-param: BonfireWarpParam via scripts/maptiles/extract-graces-param.py (regulation.bin 2.6.2 -> BonfireWarpParam + WorldMapLegacyConvParam). Exact.
sources.mapgenie-fit: MapGenie's own rows of public/data/*-locations.json pushed through a per-layer 4-parameter similarity fitted against BonfireWarpParam; ~10 px median, ~29 px p95 residual, which is MapGenie's own icon scatter rather than fit error.
sources.game-param: скриптов и расстановки самой игры. У боя - событие EMEVD, которое ставит флаг победы, называет сущность босса (HandleBossDefeat или ожидание смерти), а MSB - её место; если флаг - флаг подбора награды, то же событие находится через лот. У осколка и праха - лот из ItemLotParam (сверенная таблица DLC_COLLECTIBLE_LOTS) и то, что его выдаёт: сокровище MSB, событие или враг (NpcParam.itemLotId_enemy). Имена врагов не участвуют вовсе. Подгонки под чужую карту здесь нет: координата приходит из игры и переводится в кадр его собственной формулой. Поле `placement` говорит, ЧТО именно за точка: `world` - место под открытым небом, `underworld` - подземный слой m12, `entrance` - вход в подземелье (комнаты на карте мира нет, и метка стоит там, где игра рисует вход), `arena` - подземелье без своей иконки входа, `entry` - карта, которой на карте мира нет, и метка там, откуда игра в неё переносит. Как именно найдено - в `positionedBy`. Совпавшие у одного входа разведены по кругу в 18 px и помечены `fanned`.
sources.msb-region: региона расстановки самой игры (map/mapstudio/*.msb.dcx). Точное положение: это не подгонка, а координата, по которой игра и создаёт объект. Используется духовными источниками, которых нет ни на игровой карте, ни в параметрах.
sources.local-row-fit: a HAND-ADDED row of public/data/*-locations.json (id >= 900000, outside MapGenie's own numbering) through the same transform. The transform is identical to mapgenie-fit; the accuracy claim is NOT, and does not carry over: every number in it was fitted against rows MapGenie placed, and these rows MapGenie does not have - which is the very reason they were added by hand. Their positional accuracy is unmeasured. What is asserted instead is corroboration from the game's own data, re-checked every build: the app tracks the thing, and the pin lands inside the overworld tile the app's flag id encodes (localInputRows.kept[].verifiedAtBuildTime). Markers from this source also carry localRow: true and say so in their note.
sources.worldmappoint-param: WorldMapPointParam via scripts/maptiles/extract-locations-param.py (regulation.bin 2.6.2 -> WorldMapPointParam + WorldMapLegacyConvParam + the PlaceName FMG). Exact, in the same sense bonfire-param is: this is the position the game itself draws the icon at, reached through the same conversion chain the grace extractor walks, and NOTHING here goes through the MapGenie similarity transform - so the ~10 px scatter quoted for mapgenie-fit is not part of these positions and neither are its failure modes. What it does share with every other marker on the DLC sheet is the art-frame offset README 10.8 leaves open.

names.what: какой текст стоит в name/nameRu и откуда он взят. Имя - это то, что метка ПОКАЗЫВАЕТ; соединения идут по числам (flagId, mapGenieId, appFlagId), см. "joins".
names.grace: PlaceName игры по BonfireWarpParam.textId1 - он же placeNameId метки (у слитых меток placeNameIds перечисляет все ряды). Из игры взято 419 английских имён из 419; общинная таблица Paramdex (shortName) осталась запасным вариантом и сработала 0 раз. Русское имя - rusru PlaceName той же строки (419), запасной вариант - src/data/ru-names.ts (0), без имени 0.
names.poi: PlaceName игры по WorldMapPointParam.textId1 - он же placeNameId метки; оба языка приходят из extract-locations-param.py вместе со строкой, наших словарей в этом слое нет вовсе.
names.boss: имя из каталога приложения (BASE_GAME_BOSSES / DLC_BOSSES), иначе заголовок ряда MapGenie; русское - из src/data/ru-names.ts. 182 из 222 совпадают со строкой NpcName игры дословно, остальные - составные («Crucible Knight & Misbegotten Warrior») и уточнённые местом, каких игра одной строкой не знает.

names.note: дайджесты выгрузки игровых строк лежат здесь, а не в inputs, потому что самих выгрузок в репозитории нет (.gitignore) и тест свежести, читающий каждый файл из inputs, споткнулся бы о них на любой машине без распакованной игры. layerRouting.bosses: transform frame membership, tie-broken by which layer has a z6 tile on disk

joins.grace: flagId - the game's own BonfireWarpParam.eventflagId, which is also the key of the app's BASE_GAME_GRACES / DLC_GRACES. Merged markers carry every row's flag in flagIds.
joins.boss: flagId where the app tracks the boss, and mapGenieId always. The app's BASE_GAME_BOSSES / DLC_BOSSES carry both keys. A marker with flagIds instead of flagId is one HAND_FLAGGED_BOSSES names: an encounter the game holds no arena row for, whose defeat flags were read out of the map's EMEVD and are matched with OR because the encounter has more than one ending. Markers with neither are MapGenie boss rows the app does not track at all.
joins.scadutree-fragment: mapGenieId, and ONLY mapGenieId. These pickups have no usable save flag in the general case - SCADUTREE_FRAGMENT_FLAGS in src/data/dlc-map-specific.ts is deliberately empty - so the app keys them by the MapGenie location id in SCADUTREE_FRAGMENT_TRACKING, and the same id is the itemId of a manual UserProgress tick. Whatever flag a route does have belongs to that table and is deliberately NOT copied here: the flags are still being reverse-engineered, and a copy in a generated file would be a mirror that goes stale without anything noticing.
joins.revered-spirit-ash: mapGenieId, same as above. Only a minority of the 23 have a save flag at all; the rest can only ever be ticked manually, and the app knows which is which - this build does not restate it.
joins.poi: flagId - WorldMapPointParam's own discovery flag, unique across the layer and confined to 62100..62981. The app's existing save parser already reads that window through the same >= 50000 path that serves the DLC map fragments at 62080..62084, so nothing new was taught to it. NO mapGenieId and no manual tick: 218 of these have no MapGenie row at all, so there is no key to store a manual verdict under, and "discovered" is a thing the save says or does not - it is not a thing the player ticks. A marker carrying unreliableFlagId instead of flagId has a flag that is NOT a discovery bit and must not be joined on: see the Starfall Crater note on that marker.

poiCategories.what: the 32 kinds of place the location layer distinguishes, each mapped to the icon ids of WorldMapPointParam that mean it, and each belonging to exactly one of the four UI groups. Icon ids come from location-icon-taxonomy.json, which names an id after what it DRAWS - and for the ~40 one-off ids that is the place itself ("Castle Morne"), which is a label and not a category. The mapping from icon id to category is therefore this build's editorial decision, not a fact read off the game, and an icon id it does not cover fails the build rather than being drawn under whichever chip happens to be checked.
poiCategories.tiers: tier is the zoom band a category first draws at, and it exists because each pin now draws the game's own sprite: 0 = static landmark (minor Erdtrees, divine towers, Finger Ruins, Grand Lifts, colosseums, windmills, Miquella's crosses, landmarks), drawn already on the overview (z2); 1 = world anchor, from z3; 2 = destination, from z5; 3 = incidental, from z6. The app maps tier to zoom in POI_ZOOM_LADDER (src/lib/native-poi-ladder.ts), which is also where the measured icons-per-viewport that set these boundaries are recorded. A category this feed carries and the app does not recognise is drawn as tier 1.

msbCrossCheck.what: the game install's own MSB Treasure placements for these two categories (src/data/dlc-collectible-msb-coords.ts, machine-extracted) dropped into the master frame by the frame's own definition - px = (XX-28)*256 + 128 + x, py = (64-YY)*256 + 128 - z for an overworld m61_XX_YY tile - and measured against the nearest marker of the same kind. Distances in master px; the build throws past 80 px. It closes, for these two categories only, the gap README 10.8 records for bosses: a MapGenie-placed position with nothing measuring it. It does NOT check the DLC art-frame offset - the transform was fitted against param graces, which reach this frame through the same tile arithmetic, so a frame error would move both together.
msbCrossCheck.why_not_a_source: the MSB rows cannot be joined to markers by anything but proximity - 17 of the 56 are in dungeons with no overworld position at all, and the five Enir-Ilim fragments share one MapGenie pin - so using proximity to CHOOSE a position would be circular. Measuring agreement is not.
msbCrossCheck.stale_since_the_move: осколки и прах теперь стоят на координатах своих же лотов, поэтому для них эта величина обнулилась по построению. Она осталась страховкой на случай, если переезд возьмёт координату не из того лота, - и сохраняет прежний смысл для меток, оставшихся на mapgenie-fit.

mapGenieDisagreement.what: расстояние от метки, стоящей на координате ИГРЫ, до пина MapGenie, из которого она приехала раньше. Единственная сверка двух источников, оставшаяся независимой после переезда: игровые координаты и подгонка чужой карты не разделяют ни одного параметра.
mapGenieDisagreement.why_not_an_error: большое расхождение - не поломка. У боссов подземелий оно ожидаемо: игра знает комнату внутри, а метка стоит у входа, который карта рисует. У пары меток оно велико потому, что чужие пины переставлены местами (два Рыцаря Смерти, два Стража погребения) - это и была одна из причин переезда. Сборка на эту величину не падает: она её сообщает.

localInputRows.what: rows in public/data/*-locations.json numbered at or above 900000 are NOT MapGenie's (its own ids stop at 514797) - they were added by hand. Every one of them is audited in LOCAL_LOCATION_ROWS in the generator and either kept, with the evidence, or rejected into dropped[] with class "local-input-row". An undeclared one fails the build, so none can enter the map unexamined.

kept.title: Bell Bearing Hunter
kept.verifiedAtBuildTime: pin lands inside m60_42_38, the tile encoded in flag 1042380850
kept.why: the app's BASE_GAME_BOSSES tracks this boss by this very id (mapGenieId 900009, flag 1042380850); the flag encodes overworld tile m60_42_38 and the pin lands on that tile within one MapGenie scatter-width of its edge (asserted at build time); that tile is Warmaster's Shack, 41 px away, where the Bell Bearing Hunter actually spawns; and MapGenie's scrape has no Bell Bearing Hunter row at all, so this fills a real hole. dropped.what: the complete list of things this build was offered or is expected to draw and deliberately does NOT draw, each with a class, a POPULATION and a reason. The populations are listed in "populations" below with the assertion that keeps each complete; every entry belongs to exactly one, and the build throws if the entries do not partition across them with the count each population's own source predicts. Class and population are DIFFERENT axes and neither implies the other: "no-map-position" occurs in two populations, because the game gives no map position both to a grace it does ship a BonfireWarpParam row for (Roundtable Hold) and to one it ships no row for at all (Chapel of Anticipation) - only the first is a param row, and the param sum in the generator subtracts the second precisely because it is not. An earlier version of this text filed both under the param population, which left one of these entries in no declared population at all - and that undeclared population was the one nothing asserted. NOT in scope, because neither is a candidate that could be lost: MapGenie's own grace rows, which are only a positional index for the name joins - graces come from the param, and the param population accounts for every param row; and MapGenie boss rows the app does not track, which DO become markers, they just carry no flagId.

dropped.joinOn: appFlagId, not flagId. flagId is the game's own BonfireWarpParam.eventflagId; appFlagId is the key the same thing has in the app's tables (src/data/base-game-graces.ts, dlc-graces.ts, base-game-bosses.ts, dlc-bosses.ts). They agree everywhere except Roundtable Hold, which the game ships as eventflagId 71190 while the app tracks it as the always-unlocked sentinel { flagId: -1, name: "Table of Lost Grace" } - so a join on flagId silently misses exactly the entry most worth surfacing. Both keys are emitted, appFlagId is derived from the app tables (not hardcoded), and the build asserts that only the declared sentinel needs the name path and that every grace MARKER's flagId is a real key in those tables, so a second divergence fails the build instead of shipping an unjoinable row. Entries of class "local-input-row" carry no appFlagId on purpose: a rejected pin is not a thing the app tracks. Where one names something the app does track, "coveredBy" points at the entry that does carry the key. Entries of the two collectible populations carry neither: those pickups have no usable save flag at all, so their key is mapGenieId and it is emitted as such - see "joins".

classes.hidden-from-map: a BonfireWarpParam row with no dispMask bit at all - the game itself never draws it
classes.cut-content: a BonfireWarpParam row that is not a grace the game ships (no PlaceName string, no map, no conv row)
classes.no-map-position: a real place the game gives no world-map position for. The one to surface in a UI: name, Russian name, flag id and region, but no coordinates, because an invented one would be a lie. Read "population" as well as this class: it occurs in "param-row" (the game ships a warp row and still places it nowhere), in "app-grace-no-param-row" (the game ships no warp row at all, so the grace is not in graces-from-param.json to begin with) and in "location-param-row" (a WorldMapPointParam row whose area has no WorldMapLegacyConvParam row, so it reaches no overworld tile - one row, dead DLC content, nameless in all 21 languages)
classes.no-icon: a WorldMapPointParam location row with iconId 0: the game itself draws no icon for it. Seven of the eight also target no map sheet at all
classes.no-sheet: a WorldMapPointParam location row with an icon but no dispMask bit - the game routes it to no map sheet. Empty today: every such row also has iconId 0 and is filed under "no-icon" first. The class exists so that a patch splitting the two cases lands somewhere declared
classes.no-marker-source: a real thing the app tracks that this build has no coordinate source for. For a boss: no param holds boss positions and MapGenie has no row for it, and mapCell names the overworld tile its flag id encodes, which is as precise as the evidence goes. For a Scadutree Fragment or Revered Spirit Ash: no MapGenie row carries the mapGenieId the app tracks it by. Read "population" to tell which - the three populations that use this class are asserted separately
classes.local-input-row: a hand-added row in a *-locations.json that the audit rejected: not a place of its claimed category in the game's data, the app's tables or MapGenie's numbering

entries.name: Fire Prelate
entries.why: Прелат огня - рядовой возрождающийся враг. Три независимые проверки: (1) в NpcParam одиннадцать строк «Fire Prelate», в MSB семь расстановок на четырёх картах, и четыре из них стоят ГРУППОЙ в одной точке m60_52_55 (боссов по четыре в куче не бывает); (2) флага победы нет ни в GameAreaParam, ни в событиях карты - игра его смерть не запоминает; (3) добыча падает с шансом 4-5 % и БЕЗ getItemFlagId, то есть её можно фармить, что возможно только с возрождающегося врага.

WorldMapPointParam gives this row iconId 0, so the game itself draws no icon for it, and it names no place either: textId1 -1 has no PlaceName string. entries.why: the ruins are real, the grace is not: the game's grace there is "Yelough Anix Tunnel" (flag 73211), shipped by MapGenie as row 167154, 108 px from this pin.

entries.name: Chapel of Anticipation
entries.why: the grace is real (the app tracks flag 71010) but this pin is not its position - it sits 23 px from the Stranded Graveyard grace, a different map. The grace is carried instead as a no-map-position entry, which is where its flag id lives.

entries.name: Divine Tower of Caelid
entries.why: the tower is real, the grace name is not: the game ships "Divine Tower of Caelid: Basement" (73440) and ": Center" (73441) and MapGenie already has both (166660, 165621), 11 px and 12 px from this pin.
